g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the 30-minute reward before the opt-in game; the decline and ad-failure fields leave reading unchanged.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is a 30-minute break from sponsored cards, not cash or a transferable benefit.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger uses an article-open counter and a return to the home feed, not chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The adds and decline fields leave free reading, saving, and sharing available.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a banner on the content-safe s01 home feed, above the first story.

c1_revealed_value.reason: As a product change, the ad-free window benefits the player while reading stories in observed core flow f01.

c2_evidence.reason: The what-makes-it-work-here field claims AOL shows a full-screen video ad after every third article, which no product-model element supports. It also turns the home-feed observation that no paywall, limit, or currency was seen into an app-wide claim that none exists.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The product model shows no paid plan, and the subscribers field proposes withholding the banner from members if an ad-free plan is added.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 30 minutes and does not take a placement or benefit from another user or creator.

c5_moment.reason: The trigger places the banner on the home feed after the reader returns from an article, rather than during the read.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The flow grants the break once play is confirmed, and the failure path grants nothing when confirmation fails; returning to the feed is a detectable app event.

c7_specific.reason: The idea uses s01’s category pills and the sponsored placements observed at s01.e44, s06.e33, and s02.e13.

other_concern: The proposed trade-off between playable revenue and hidden-card revenue needs validation; the model establishes placement and variable fill, not ad value.
